title: Week 01 - Variables
description: Practice sequential calculation, variable updates, variable swapping, and addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulo operations.

questions.title: How Much Health Is Left After a Game Character Is Attacked
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

A game character enters a level with some initial health. After battle starts, a monster attacks the character once and deals fixed damage. The system needs to update the character's current health after the attack so it can later decide whether the character can keep fighting.

## Task

Calculate the remaining health after the attack from the character's original health and the damage taken this time.

## Input

Two numbers: hp and damage, representing the character's initial health and the damage taken this time.

## Output

Return the character's remaining health after the attack.

## Hint

You can save the updated health in a variable first, then return that variable.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(hp, damage)
    local remainHp = hp - damage
    return remainHp
end

questions.title: How Much Do the Pencils Cost at the Stationery Store
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

A stationery store sells one kind of pencil at the same price per pencil. A student plans to buy several pencils and needs to know the total amount to pay before checkout.

## Task

Calculate the total cost of this pencil purchase from the unit price and quantity.

## Input

Two numbers: price and count, representing the price of each pencil and the quantity purchased.

## Output

Return the total amount to pay for these pencils.

## Hint

You can save the total price in a variable first, then return that variable.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(price, count)
    local total = price * count
    return total
end

questions.title: What Is the Area of the Rectangular Playground
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

A rectangular training area has been marked on the school playground. The PE teacher needs to know how large this area is to arrange student groups and equipment placement.

## Task

Calculate the area of the training area from its length and width.

## Input

Two numbers: length and width, representing the length and width of the rectangular area.

## Output

Return the area of this rectangular training area.

## Hint

You can save the calculated area in a variable first, then return the result.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(length, width)
    local area = length * width
    return area
end

questions.title: How Many Coins Are in the Bag After Defeating a Monster
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

A game character originally has some coins in the bag. After defeating a monster, the character receives a new coin reward. The system needs to add this reward to the bag and update the current coin count.

## Task

Calculate the updated coin total from the original coin count and the reward earned this time.

## Input

Two numbers: coins and reward, representing the original coin count and the newly earned coin reward.

## Output

Return the total number of coins after receiving the reward.

## Hint

You can use a new variable to represent the updated coin count.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(coins, reward)
    local totalCoins = coins + reward
    return totalCoins
end

questions.title: How Much Money Is Left After Buying Pencils and Erasers
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

A student brings a fixed amount of money to a stationery store. The student plans to buy several pencils and several erasers. The unit prices and quantities for both items are known, and the student needs to know how much money will be left after checkout.

## Task

Calculate the cost of the pencils and the cost of the erasers separately, then calculate the remaining amount after shopping.

## Input

Five numbers: money, pencilPrice, pencilCount, eraserPrice, and eraserCount, representing the total money, pencil unit price, pencil quantity, eraser unit price, and eraser quantity.

## Output

Return the amount of money left after buying these stationery items.

## Hint

You can save the costs of the two stationery items separately, then subtract those costs from the total money.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(money, pencilPrice, pencilCount, eraserPrice, eraserCount)
    local pencilTotal = pencilPrice * pencilCount
    local eraserTotal = eraserPrice * eraserCount
    local leftMoney = money - pencilTotal - eraserTotal
    return leftMoney
end

questions.title: How Many Meters Have Been Run After Training
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

An athlete records accumulated running distance every day. Before today's training starts, there is already an accumulated distance; after today's training ends, a new running distance is added. The coach needs to update the athlete's accumulated training data.

## Task

Calculate the accumulated running distance after training from the previous accumulated distance and today's added distance.

## Input

Two numbers: beforeMeters and todayMeters, representing the accumulated distance before training and the distance added today.

## Output

Return the accumulated running distance after training.

## Hint

You can save the new accumulated distance in a variable first, then return the result.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(beforeMeters, todayMeters)
    local totalMeters = beforeMeters + todayMeters
    return totalMeters
end

questions.title: Update the Seat Statistics Card After Two Students Swap Seats
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

Two students in a classroom temporarily swap seats. The teacher needs to record the swapped seat numbers on a seat statistics card and also calculate the sum, difference, average, and a remainder code for group checking. This record will be used later to verify whether the seat adjustment is correct.

## Task

First swap the two students' seat numbers, then use the swapped numbers to complete several statistics calculations.

## Input

Three numbers: seatA, seatB, and groupSize, representing the two students' original seat numbers and the group size used for checking.

## Output

Return six values: swapped seatA, swapped seatB, the seat number sum, the seat number average, the difference between the two seat numbers, and the group-check remainder.

## Hint

This problem uses addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulo. In Lua, the modulo operator is %. Pay attention to operator precedence: multiplication, division, and modulo usually run before addition and subtraction. For complex calculations, split the work into multiple variables.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(seatA, seatB, groupSize)
    local temp = seatA
    seatA = seatB
    seatB = temp
    local total = seatA + seatB
    local average = total / 2
    local gap = seatA - seatB
    local checkCode = seatA * seatB
    local remainder = checkCode % groupSize
    return seatA, seatB, total, average, gap, remainder
end

questions.title: Final Health Settlement After Consecutive Battles
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

A game character enters consecutive battles with some health. During battle, the character takes multiple attacks; after battle ends, the character uses several potions to restore health. In addition to basic healing, the potions create extra healing according to a rule. The system also needs to calculate the remainder code used to display the final health by group.

## Task

Follow the battle process in order: handle total damage, potion healing, bonus healing, and final-health grouping, then return the final health and group remainder.

## Input

Four numbers: hp, damage, heal, and potionCount, representing initial health, damage per attack, basic healing per potion, and the number of potions used.

## Output

Return two values: the final health and the group remainder for that final health.

## Hint

Split this problem into steps: process damage first, then healing, and finally modulo. Pay attention to operator precedence, especially multiplication, division, and modulo. Do not squeeze all calculations into one line.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(hp, damage, heal, potionCount)
    local currentHp = hp
    local totalDamage = damage * 2
    currentHp = currentHp - totalDamage
    local totalHeal = heal * potionCount
    local bonusHeal = totalHeal / 2
    currentHp = currentHp + totalHeal + bonusHeal
    local remainder = currentHp % potionCount
    return currentHp, remainder
end

questions.title: Store Bundle Discount, Packaging Fee, and Change Settlement
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

A store is selling one kind of bundle, and each bundle has the same price. A student brings some money and buys several bundles. At checkout, the cashier needs to calculate the original total price first, then calculate the promotion discount. Bundles are packed in fixed-size groups, and loose bundles that cannot make a complete group create an extra packaging fee. Finally, the cashier needs to calculate the change from the student's payment.

## Task

Complete the full checkout process: calculate the original total, promotion discount, loose bundle count, packaging fee, discounted payable amount, and change.

## Input

Three numbers: money, packPrice, and packCount, representing the student's payment, bundle unit price, and purchase quantity.

## Output

Return four values: the discounted payable amount, the change, the average discounted amount per bundle, and the loose bundle count.

## Hint

This problem uses addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulo. Pay attention to operator precedence.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(money, packPrice, packCount)
    local total = packPrice * packCount
    local discount = total / 10
    local looseCount = packCount % 3
    local packageFee = looseCount * 1
    local finalTotal = total - discount + packageFee
    local change = money - finalTotal
    local average = finalTotal / packCount
    return finalTotal, change, average, looseCount
end
